sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational sample augmented by deterministic public nuisance functions \((m_0,m_1,p)\), supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) error radii bounded by \(\bar r\), a fixed signal envelope \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\), and decision rules that may use all public inputs.
sampling_model.units: Independent units \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), from a causal law satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with propensity \(e(X)\), positive almost surely and allowed to approach zero.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform one-sided dyadic shells satisfy \(c_-u^\kappa\le P\{u/2<e(X)\le u\}\le c_+u^\kappa\) for \(0<u\le\lambda_0\), while \(e(X)\le1-\eta_+\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The minimax infima range over rules measurable in \(O^{(n)}\) that also receive \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\).  The same public inputs are fixed within each lower family, the certified radii lie in \([0,\bar r]\), and the lower witness uses finite equal-cell refinements of an explicit countable atomic reservoir.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bound in the paper's estimator-bounded class; for constant weight, the interpretive squared-radius mapping yields \(n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}\), while Remark 2 retains the treated-side lower-bound form with known baseline response.

Section 2 gives the lower-rate form \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\) for one mean functional in its pure structure-agnostic class; it does not attest a control-arm extension, a joint two-arm ATE equivalence, or a matching upper bound for the comparator class in this note.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Extreme propensity scores generate non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

body.tldr: Global prediction accuracy does not determine the attainable accuracy of the full-population ATE when treated observations become polynomially rare.  In the public-function experiment with bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates, a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, and uniform one-sided propensity shells, the exact minimax rate is the four-channel quantity \(\rho_n\): tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden in shells with no treated observations, localized propensity--treated-regression uncertainty, and the regular control-side nuisance interaction.  An explicit atomic dyadic reservoir now certifies every fixed-sign lower law and the exact \(\kappa=1\) logarithm.  A clipped doubly robust average, a five-block median, and a bias-aware interval attain the matching absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability, and honest-length frontiers.  Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published regular-overlap structure-agnostic results provide lower-bound templates, but the attested BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE passage concerns only one mean functional and does not supply a control-arm or joint two-arm ATE theorem.  Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than one matched four-risk frontier.  The accepted-bank result \(\texttt{stat\_policy\_regret\_margin\_overlap\_v1}\) studies margin-localized policy-welfare regret under coupled Tsybakov margin and one-sided-overlap decay, and \(\texttt{stat\_lmtp\_threshold\_atom\_frontier\_v1}\) studies a continuous-exposure clamp functional under finite-stratum polynomial thinning.  Their targets and classes do not subsume the present binary-treatment full-ATE experiment, and the present experiment does not subsume theirs.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model isolates the statistical price of knowing only global prediction-error guarantees when the treated design vanishes at a boundary.  The left tail creates three distinct treated-side obstructions, while the control-side product remains regular; a fixed \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) condition keeps the ATE finite without a pointwise outcome envelope.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the explicit decision classes, clipped and median estimators, bias-aware interval, and a law-by-law four-channel converse.  The converse uses the atomic reservoir \(t_j=s_0 2^{-j}\), \(w_j=A(1-2^{-\kappa})t_j^\kappa\), proves its exact tail and treated-mass sums, constructs moving and fixed equal-cell bands, and verifies positivity, right overlap, shell caps, nuisance radii, moments, cancellation, collisions, and the \(\kappa=1\) logarithm before combining the channels into \(\rho_n\).

body.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1, gives a squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bound in its own estimator-bounded class; Remark 2 retains a treated-side known-baseline lower-bound form.  BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, states only that no estimator of its single mean functional \(\psi\) over its pure structure-agnostic class is faster than \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\).  The attested passage supplies neither a control-arm extension nor a joint two-arm ATE equivalence.  The fast-tail limit of the present rate has the same parametric-plus-treated-product algebraic form after the stated radius identification, which is only a sanity comparison and not a class transfer.  Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics, MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, MaWang2020RobustIPW, and HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity study Gaussian or non-Gaussian inference, trimming, or threshold selection rather than this matched public-function minimax frontier.  KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies a fuzzy-hypothesis template for a different estimand and smoothness class; KhanTamer2010Irregular explains the tail-driven inverse-weight obstruction; Rothe2017RobustCI studies limited-overlap coverage under finite-cell or auxiliary structure.  Within the accepted bank, \(\texttt{stat\_policy\_regret\_margin\_overlap\_v1}\) concerns policy welfare regret localized by a Tsybakov margin, with a coupled one-sided-overlap exponent and conditional ERM achievability assumptions; it is not a full-population ATE result under global public \(L^2\) certificates.  The accepted \(\texttt{stat\_lmtp\_threshold\_atom\_frontier\_v1}\) concerns an exact continuous-exposure clamp functional in finite-stratum polynomial-thinning Hölder or continuity classes, a threshold atom, and a separate causal-transport bridge; it is not binary-treatment ATE or a four-nuisance-channel result.  Neither accepted-bank class or target subsumes this theorem, and this theorem does not subsume either accepted result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The converse uses reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness.  Its active reservoir is no longer existential: level \(j\) has propensity \(t_j=s_0 2^{-j}\) and mass \(w_j=A(1-2^{-\kappa})t_j^\kappa\), with \(0<A\le(c_+-2^\kappa c_-)/2^{\kappa+1}\); each finite experiment uses distinct equal-mass measurable points.  Exact geometric sums give active tail mass of order \(v^\kappa\), treated mass of order \(v^{\kappa+1}\), and a fixed band of positive mass.  Treated fuzzy propensities have ratios in \([4/5,4/3]\), control fuzzy propensities in \([3/4,5/4]\), and the active contribution consumes at most half the shell slack.  At \(\kappa=1\), the proof uses the exact dyadic sums for \(\|f\|_2^2\), \(E[e_0f^2]\), and \(E[f]\), not density or integral heuristics.  The upper bound needs no reservoir richness, so arbitrarily tight admissible shell constants may have different converse geometry.
body.honest_scope: The theorem concerns supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and the primitive signal condition \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\); it imposes no pointwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or Gaussian-limit claim.  Every minimax rule may use all supplied public inputs.  The confidence interval is bias-aware and oracle-calibrated.  Adaptation to unknown shell constants, tail exponent, and nuisance radii, bounded-outcome variants, arbitrary shell constants, and exact studentized validity remain open.  The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp papers are non-nested in both target and class.  The fast-tail expression is a rate-form comparison to verified published lower-bound templates, not a transferred regular-class minimax theorem.
body.interpretation: The regular-benchmark reduction is only an algebraic check: as \(\kappa\to\infty\), the treated side has the same parametric-plus-product form as the two verified published lower-bound templates after their explicit radius identifications.  Bonvini's attested one-functional statement is used only for the treated-side mapping \(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\), \(\delta_n=r_{en}\); no control-arm term is attributed to that source.  The shell class and the regular comparator class are disjoint, so the calculation establishes neither minimax equivalence nor inclusion transfer.  The accepted policy-regret and clamp-functional frontiers answer different causal decision problems under different law classes.
